units.title: call outs
units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Two nights, three call outs, and I've had about five hours sleep total. Coast road feeder trips around eleven, we patrol, find nothing, test it, close it in, back to the depot, then it goes again. Management says salt. I've washed salt off insulators for twenty five years and I know what a tracking fault does. Not saying it isn't. Saying I'm flaming tired.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Patrol notes from last night for anyone who's curious. Walked poles 41 to 77 with Garvey from 23:40 with the big torch. No flashover marks on the insulators. No birds on the line, no branches, nothing hanging. Frost on the conductors. The trip recorder showed the first trip near the Brackwater end and the reclose fault further toward Gilliver. Like it moved.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: lads I had the chandlery freezers go off twice this week and I'm not complaining to you about it because I know you're up a pole in the dark. get some sleep garvey. tess dont get carried away on here, management read this board too

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Fair, Rook. I'll keep it to what I saw. I just like writing things down, it's how I learn. Garvey says if I'm going to post patrol notes I should at least spell 'insulator' right, which I didn't the first time, so that's been edited.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: From the engine room, so take it as a mechanic's view: a fault that 'moves' along a line on the recorder usually means the recorder is estimating distance from impedance, and that estimate is rubbish when the fault is high-resistance, like a damp film. Wouldn't read much into the movement. Would read plenty into Garvey being knackered.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Seth makes the point I was going to. Fault location on a high-resistance fault is notoriously approximate. And a clean-looking insulator in torchlight isn't necessarily a clean insulator; the film that causes tracking is invisible until it fails. None of what Tess describes contradicts salt. I'd want a daylight inspection with a cloth before I ruled it out.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Did the daylight inspection today, with a cloth, Ferrous, poles 41 to 60. Some salt, aye, normal for the coast in winter, nothing I'd expect to trip on a dry night. And last night was dry. I'll say it once and then I'll shut up: it isn't corrosion. The breakers are tripping like something's leaning on the line. Heavy, slow, then letting go.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: I respect twenty-five years more than I respect a press release, Garvey, genuinely. So: what would we expect to see if something were leaning on the line? Sag, marks on the conductor, a disturbed pole, damage at the binding. Did you find any of that? If not, 'leaning' is a description of how the trip feels on the recorder, not a cause.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: No. Nothing. No sag, no marks, bindings tight, frost undisturbed on the crossarms. You're right that it's how it looks on the trace. Current climbs, holds, climbs, trips. That's what a tree on the line does. There's no tree. That's all I've got. I'm not going to make anything else of it, and neither should anyone else.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Pint on me Friday, mate. You and Ferrous can draw traces on beer mats. For what it's worth, a load that climbs and holds could be a big motor somewhere starting on the feeder, a farm with a grain dryer, a pump station. Worth asking who's on that line who runs things at night.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Good idea, Seth. I checked: on the coast road feeder there's the care home, the Gilliver ice plant, the harbour substation, two farms and the old pumping station, which has been off since the summer. Ice plant's off at night. Care home's steady. I'll ask the farms. If it's a grain dryer, I'll be very happy and very embarrassed.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Garvey knows lines like I know the Holm tides. If he says it's not salt, I'd want a good reason to say otherwise. That said, my father always reckoned the coast road line hummed louder on still nights. Never knew why. Probably nothing.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Farms answered. One has no dryer, one has a dryer that hasn't run since October. So that's not it. Last night the inland feeder tripped instead, first time this week. Same shape on the recorder Garvey described. I walked a stretch with the duty crew at one. Nothing on the line. Very quiet up there, no wind at all.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: The office has had a word about posting on public forums, so I'll keep it to what we do, not what I think. We wash the insulators. We patrol the line. We write it down. Tess, keep doing what you're doing. Rook, sorry about your freezers. Back on nights tonight.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: fair enough garvey. management can read this then: your lads have been out every night this week in minus five and nobody on this board has a bad word for them. dont care what it is, salt or whatever, just keep the lights on. thread stays open

units.title: night boats: anyone know how long
units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Asking for the pier, ha, because people keep asking me and I don't know... How long are the night boats off for? Last crossing in at 19:40 now and then the pier's just me and the gulls till I lock up. Nobody's told me anything except 'review'. It's very quiet down there without the 22:10.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: till the lights are fitted ada is what odell told me. lighting comes on the van from weyhaven, then it goes on in the yard. week maybe. the lads need the break anyway

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Rook has it about right. Lights first, then nights. I'm not going to discuss the review on here beyond saying it was the right call and the crew asked for it. We're running extra daytime checks on the slips meanwhile. Ada, thank you for keeping the pier lit after the last boat. Noticed, logged it.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: What the skipper said. I'm not going over it all again on here, I've said what I saw and it hasn't changed. Tall, dark coat, no light, end of the slip where the water starts. Two hails. I'll say it as many times as people need. The lights are a good idea. That's all I want to say.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Kerris, nobody's asking you to... sorry, I didn't mean to start anything. I only wanted to know about the timetable, honestly. I leave the pier lights on till I'm in my car now, all of them. I don't know why I'm telling everyone that. Ha. Anyway.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Technical bit, since it's me: the new kit is two LED floods per vessel on the wheelhouse roof, aimed aft and down over the passenger deck, plus a pair of shore floods at each slip on twelve metre poles. Generator-backed at the slips so they stay on in a cut. Fitting starts on the Lisle Maid in the yard next week.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: ada nobody's cross with you love. kerris neither. right, i'm locking this one before it goes round again. timetable updates go in the ferry notices thread, odell's said what he can say and theres nothing more to add about the review on here

units.title: ice on the slip and whats in the shop
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: frost coming lads. in the chandlery: rock salt, deck grit, de-icer for winches, hand warmers, thermals in L and XL only, lamp oil (going fast), hurricane lamp glasses, wicks. bring your own bags. if youre on the slip at low water this week mind the bottom section, its like glass

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you, Rook. A reminder to all harbour users that under byelaw 9 the slipway must be kept clear of gear and catch at all times, and under byelaw 14 the lower section is for authorised use only. Harbour staff will salt the slipway approach twice daily during the frost warning. Please report ice on the pontoon steps to the office.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Creels froze to the deck this morning, had to pour the kettle on them. Hands no use till ten. Prices at the market fair, crab up a bit because nobody else went out. Rook, put me down for a bottle of lamp oil before it's gone, Maud's been through hers.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: lamp oil all gone, sorry bram, last bottle went at four yesterday to a woman from lisle who bought six. never sold out in my life. more on the van next week. radio people rang me about it this morning. told them its winter and the powers going off, not complicated

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: That'll have been Mrs Pengelly from the top of the hill, she buys everything in sixes. She told me on the morning boat she wants one lamp for every window facing the water. I didn't ask. Lisle's like that this week.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: She's done it too, Kerris, you can see them from the pier, a whole row of little yellow windows going up the hill. It's actually lovely. Ha. I counted eleven houses with a lamp lit on the Lisle side last night. There's usually two.

units.title: lights on the holm
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Out on the creel line by five. Flat calm. The camp lights on the Holm were fewer than usual this morning. Four, maybe five, where there's been eight or nine every morning since they started. Steady, not flickering. They'll have moved camp or be saving fuel. Just saying what I saw. I'll ring Maud, she watches them from her window.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: generator rationing probably. the supply boat had a short load last trip, the fuel depot pump has been playing up since the first cut. dont make it a thing bram, sound board will have it as a mystery by dinner

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Not making it a thing. Short load would do it. Fair enough. Would still rather see eight than four out there, that's all. Nobody's ever had a light on the Holm at night in my life and I'm used to looking at it now.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: For information: the supply vessel working the Holm landing is in regular contact with this office, as all working vessels are. Its skipper reported nothing unusual on his last crossing. The Coastguard has issued a notice so that mariners do not confuse the camp lights with navigation lights. Thank you.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: From the ferry, on daytime runs, you can see where they've been working at the Holm's north end: gaps opening in the trees along the shore, stacks by the landing, smoke some days from what I'd guess is a burn pit. It looks like a working job. Fewer lights likely means they've moved them to where the work is. Observed, nothing to log.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Not my area at all, but for what it's worth: the Holm's not on our network, they'll be on their own generator, so none of this week's cuts would touch them. Whatever's going on with their lights is their own business. Sorry Bram, I know you just meant you were looking out for them.

units.title: ledge buoy out
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Ledge buoy light's been out since the storm, near enough a week. Nobody's said owt till now. Daymark's fine but that's no use at five in the morning. Anyone going out the Holm side in the dark, keep wide of the ledge. I know it blind, but not everyone does.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you, Bram. I've reported it to the Coastguard this morning and a notice to mariners has been issued. The lantern will be replaced when the tide allows the tender alongside, probably later this week given the calm. Apologies that it took a forum post to bring it to the office's attention.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Noted on our bridge. We don't pass the ledge on the ferry route, but the supply boat to the Holm does, and he's crossing in the last of the light now. I've let him know. Calm water helps. Logged it.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: tender went out at slack water this afternoon, new lantern on. saw it flashing from the shop at four. thanks quill. thats one light this week that came back on when it was supposed to

units.title: market prices and the cold
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Brown crab steady, lobster down with the restaurants quiet, velvets nobody wants. Diesel up four cents at the pump since the storm. Forecast flat calm for days, which is grand for the creels and hard on the fingers. Gloves wanted, size large, if anybody's got a spare pair that aren't full of holes.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: gloves in the shop bram, the orange ones, you know where. diesel will go up again with the cold, everyone wants it for heating. tell the restaurants to stop being quiet. velvets are good fried, nobody listens to me

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Diesel tip for anyone with an older boat or a cabin heater: add the anti-gel before the cold, not after. Once it's waxed in the filter you'll be on your back in the bilge with a hairdryer, and believe me, it's not as romantic as it sounds. We dosed all three ferries yesterday.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Dosed mine last night on your say so, Seth. Started first pull at half four this morning at minus three. Owe you a crab. Calm as a millpond out there, could hear every bird on the Holm shore from the line. Never heard it that quiet.

units.title: anyone heard from finn
units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Not asking anyone to say anything they shouldn't. Just: has anyone seen Finn since he packed it in? He left his good socks and a flask in the crew room and I'd like to get them back to him. He's not answering texts, which is fair enough. If you see him, tell him the engine room says hello and the flask is safe.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: seen him on the harbour wall yesterday seth, he's alright, quiet, says he might go on his cousins boat after christmas. i'll leave the flask behind my counter if you drop it in. dont pester him lads

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: He's fine. I saw him too. He just wants to be left alone for a bit and he doesn't want people asking him about it. I'd ask everyone to do what he asked and not go over his post. He did nothing wrong. He was a good deckhand.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Understood, nobody will hear it from me. Flask and socks are behind Rook's counter. The socks have been washed. I want that on the record as an act of great personal sacrifice.

units.title: inner harbour skinned over
units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: For information: thin ice formed overnight across the inner harbour basin, first time since the winter of the big freeze. It will not bear weight. Please keep children and dogs off the steps and pontoons. Vessels leaving the inner basin may break it; please proceed slowly to avoid damage to moored craft. Thank you.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Went through it at half four like cutting a loaf. Sounded like breaking glass all the way out. My father said the basin froze the year before I was born and men walked out to the moorings. Don't anyone try it.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Port Ammet's outer harbour is too salty and too stirred up to freeze, but we've got rime on every rail on the boat this morning, half an inch, like the ship's grown fur. Deckhands chipping it off the gangway with a spade. The sea smoke off the water at sunrise was something, mind.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: walk out to the moorings and i'll ban you from the shop for life. thats a promise lads. also kettle on in the back for anyone coming off the water, its too cold to be proud
